thread.title_full: From $0.17 to Paying My Bills With Writing

author: Cosmin Angheluta
title: From $0.17 to Paying My Bills With Writing
text:
Want to Monetize Your Passion? Answer These 5 Questions First — Preview This is my 100th free newsletter on Substack. It took me two years to get here, but I did it.
I thought about this post for a while now. I wanted to make something special. However, I also didn’t want to stray too far from my niche. So, I thought I would share the story that made The Challenge my most successful Internet project (until now).
I'd like to share with you how I leveraged my passion for writing to support myself financially . And hopefully, that could inspire you to do the same, if you haven’t started yet. Or keep going, if you’re already in the game but have many doubts about how to get ahead.
How I Started Working Online
You’ve probably heard this story many times before.
Big breakup. Your world crushes. You realize you haven’t been taking care of yourself. You decide to work on yourself and your passions.
That’s exactly what happened to me, too. I was alone, living far from my family, in a big home. I spent my evenings looking at love and relationship videos. Some of them were good advice, but the majority was a waste of time.
Then, I knew someone who was into personal growth. He was the first person who ever talked to me about that. And he gifted me a book, The Slight Edge , by Jeff Olson.
I read it. And I started reading a lot of non-fiction books. Psychology, finance, and personal growth — I liked them all. And I felt the need to share my knowledge. That’s when I discovered Medium.
My First Steps on Medium
I wrote my first article in English on February 29, 2020. It’s called The absolute power of talking to yourself , and it got me $0.17.
Every time I read it, I want to curl up and die. But I never edited it. I like to see how much progress I have made.
A few months later, I launched my self-hosted blog, Cosmopolitan Mindset , which is live today. I wanted to have a place I could call mine. And I wanted to try it to see how it was.
On 13th September 2023, I wrote my last post on Medium and my blog. I loved writing there, and I also started to make some money.
My top month got me $71.97. It was December 2023, after I stopped publishing regularly. Some of my posts went viral, and I was so proud. But I spent too much energy searching for publications that would publish the work of a small writer. I didn’t have control over what I was doing. And many times, I lost my consistency because of it.
The Transition to Substack
Substack was something I always wanted to try out. But I didn’t have enough time to write for Medium and my blog. In that period, I was always fascinated by people who made content around challenges. I used to look at many videos on YouTube of 30-day challenges. And I wanted to make something similar.
In 2023, I founded The Challenge for people who wanted more. It was one of my New Year’s resolutions, and I promoted it in my articles. But it didn’t get the results I expected.
In the first eight months, I collected 150 emails. I don’t know if that’s a lot. But for me, it wasn’t enough. My posts were short. My style was still rough. But one day, in August, I woke up and found $5 on my Stripe account.
I couldn’t believe it. Why would somebody pay for that kind of content? Apparently, it was useful to someone. And they paid for my content for more than a year. (Thank you, Marcus, if you’re reading. You started all of this, but I never had the courage to write a thank you e-mail.)
So, I went all in. At that time, I thought it was the best. And I started investing in my newsletter. I collaborated with Deepstash to promote my newsletter. My list started growing, and I felt like nothing could stop me, even if I was only making $5 a month.
After six months of consistent work, The Challenge paid for my Netflix subscription (not the best investment, I agree) .
After one year, it paid for a dinner for two.
And now, two years later, it’s paying for my Internet connection and Netflix account. Sometimes, some of you also offer dinner.
I know it’s not a lot. But all of this is happening while doing something I love. And I couldn’t feel happier. So, thank you for that.
How to Use Your Passion to Pay Your Bills
You had to read all of that, but we’re finally here. I’m not making much with this project, you saw. But The Challenge is paying part of my bills. And that is money I would not have otherwise.
So, how can you use your passion to pay your bills?
If I could talk to my younger me, these are the questions I would recommend answering.
1 — Are You Ready?
This is the first question I would ask my younger self: Are you sure you’re ready?
When you start a new project, you think about the commitments you are making. You know that if you fail, there will be consequences. But when you start a project online, the consequences don’t seem that important. Still, there will be people who will put their trust in you. And if you give up, your decision may have an impact on them.
It may take you a few days or months to get here, where I’m now. Or it might take years, as it did for me. If you’re working with passion, it shouldn’t matter. You would do that anyway. But are you sure this is your passion and not a temporary fling? And do you want to ruin it by making a job out of it? Because that’s what will happen.
You like to do it now, when there’s no pressure. Most times, you will also like it in the future. But sometimes, you may have to work after a hard day at work. All you wish to do is sleep, but you can’t.
You may go through tough times. Your creative juices might dry up. It doesn’t matter. You took a commitment, and if you ignore it, you will lose credibility.
So, are you ready for all of that? If you’re not, stay away from this.
2 — How Can You Monetize?
If you’re still reading, I guess I couldn’t stop you. Well, congratulations. You are brave and naive. But here’s the good news:
Your passion is truly a passion.
You may earn some money in the future.
Now, how do you do that?
When I started, I didn’t know what I should write about. But I had the presumption I knew how to make money online. So I made a lot of mistakes I could have avoided.
The key is to search for people who have already monetized and imitate them.
Do you have any combos of passion that nobody has explored yet? Try to find something that you like online, but also that has a different nuance. You want people to feel familiar with your content, but you also want to give them something fresh they cannot find elsewhere.
3 — Where Will You Publish?
The platform you choose can have a great impact on your success. Each of them has its peculiarities.
On Substack, you need to bring your audience from something else or build it with Substack Notes. On Medium, you have to submit your stories to publications if you want to reach a wider audience.
The platform you choose also depends on the type of content you want to make. If you’re into writing, Substack and Medium. Pick YouTube if you want to produce videos. Or you could use Etsy or Gumroad to sell your unique products and make content around them.
You can even use all of them at the same time, but I don’t recommend it. The more platforms you have, the harder it will be to stand out. You won’t have time to promote your content everywhere. You won’t study how the platform works. And you will fall behind.
4 — How Can You Remain Consistent?
When you start a new project, everything looks exciting.
You are full of motivation. You feel like you could produce content for days. And you don’t feel fatigued. But soon, reality will hit you in the face, and it will be brutal.
Writing on Medium felt incredible in the first few days. I made $0.17 overnight without an audience. Incredible! Who knows how much I could do in a month?
Well, I couldn’t do much more. February brought me $0.17 in a day. In March, I made $5. But April crushed to $0.22. I kept writing as always. I discussed the same topics and published with the same consistency. But for the algorithm, those articles were unworthy.
That realization kills your vibe. But you have to keep going. I could write a book on consistency, but if you are starting right now, you only need two things:
Practice daily. You don’t always have to produce good content, but you must produce.
Delay your decisions . I know you’ll feel down, and you will want to give up. But you shouldn’t make decisions when you’re not emotionally stable.
5 — Which Will Be Your Goals?
You should delay your decision. Great. But until when?
Let’s use your goals for that.
I set my first goal after a month of writing online. I didn’t know if that was something I wanted to do forever. I was trying out a new thing to see how things were going. But making my first dollars made me take it more seriously.
If I hadn’t set a goal, the next month would have crushed my spirit. And it didn’t happen only once — even with The Challenge, I had my fair share of disappointments. But my goals kept me going.
I always followed the two rules of consistency above and focused on my purpose. Sometimes, I made a decision based on my emotions. I would stop writing for a week or two. But my goals were always there, approaching. And that kept me going.
This year, for example, I set a goal to reach 5k subscribers by December 31, 2025. I started with 3k, and I reached 4.2k. I don’t think I will make it, but if there’s even the slightest hope, I will keep working on my goal. And if I can’t reach it, I would cheer for the progress.
For goals, as for consistency, follow these two rules:
Accept that the goals you will set will always be challenging. We have a positive bias towards the future, and you can’t do anything about it.
Break your goals into daily actions. You may forget or delay it otherwise.
The Challenge of The Month
This is how you can use your passion to pay your bills. Or, at least, that’s how I did it.
I made my mistakes. I gave up, came back, and gave up again many times. I switched platforms, abandoned projects, and followed the shiny trends. But I am still here. After more than five years, I am still writing.
You may unfollow me in a few days or months. You may stay with me forever. I don’t know what will happen. But of one thing I am certain — I will keep writing. That’s what it takes to use your passion to pay your bills.
Do you have a lifelong dream or passion? Do you think you could make money with it? Ask yourself the five questions above to find out now.
